walkthroughs.title: Food sticking and unintentional weight loss

doorway: Food is getting stuck when I swallow, and I am losing weight.
Vital signs are available on the chart.
Perform a focused history and physical examination, discuss your plan, and document only what you obtain.

plan.notice: Distinguish difficulty initiating a swallow from food sticking after swallowing; solids and liquids provide different clues.
plan.anchor: Where it sticks, what sticks, how it changes
plan.pivot: Ask progression, solids versus liquids, food impaction, pain on swallowing, reflux, atopy and weight change. Clarify inability to swallow saliva promptly.
plan.exam: Inspect the mouth and neck and assess general condition; a normal surface examination cannot establish a normal esophagus.
plan.avoid: Writing odynophagia when the patient describes painless sticking, or treating a future endoscopy as a current finding.

goals: Distinguish initiating swallowing from food sticking afterward.
Ask solids versus liquids and quantify weight loss.
Avoid reassuring away alarm symptoms with an antacid trial.

cc: Food sticking and unintentional weight loss

HPI: 26-year-old man with progressive food sticking behind the breastbone after swallowing; onset 8 weeks ago. Initially solids, now soft foods; meat and bread most difficult. Small bites and water sometimes help. Regurgitation, fatigue and unintentional loss of 10 lb over 2 months. Years of heartburn; antacid helps heartburn but not sticking. No arm/back radiation. This progressive swallowing difficulty is new.

Perspective: My father had cancer. Is that what this is?

PSH: No surgeries or admissions.

Meds: Calcium carbonate antacid; frequency not established.

Allergies: No known drug allergies.

FH: My mother is still alive, and she had a stroke when she was seventy-eight.; My father died of lung cancer when he was seventy.; I have one sister and she is healthy.

reasoning.question: Is it hard to start swallowing, or does food stick afterward; are solids, liquids or both affected?
reasoning.why: The phase and food consistency help distinguish oropharyngeal, structural and motility patterns.
reasoning.if_present: Progression from solids plus weight loss warrants prompt structural evaluation.
reasoning.if_absent: Symptoms with both solids and liquids may suggest motility, but alarm features still need investigation.
reasoning.next_action: Assess ability to manage saliva and nutrition, then arrange timely specialist evaluation.
